tools.name: create_ai_agent
tools.description: Create a complete AI Agent in one call: the agent resource plus an auto-provisioned flow, AI Agent Job Node and REST endpoint. Do not create those pieces separately. If projectId is omitted, a new project is created from the agent name. Passing knowledgeStoreReferenceId also attaches a knowledge-search tool to the Job Node. agentNodeType 'llmPrompt' (only when the user asks for an LLM Prompt node by name) builds the flow on an LLM Prompt node driven by systemPrompt, with no agent resource. Returns the agent, flow and endpoint, endpointId and hasToken (the endpoint URL and token are not returned; pass endpointId to talk_to_agent), the projectId used, and llmStatus. The agent cannot answer until the project has a working, connected LLM; llmStatus 'unknown' means that is not yet confirmed.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Optional — if omitted, a new project is created automatically.

description.description: Agent persona (max 1000 chars): who the agent is, who it serves and how it comes across, in prose. The agent-prompts skill has the layout and writing rules for every prompt field.

knowledgeStoreReferenceId.description: Optional knowledge store referenceId (from manage_knowledge create_store). When set, a knowledge-search tool for that store is created on the Job Node. Not supported with agentNodeType 'llmPrompt'.

agentNodeType.description: Which node drives the agent. Omit for the AI Agent default. Pass 'llmPrompt' only when the user asked for an LLM Prompt node by name.

systemPrompt.description: llmPrompt mode only: freeform system prompt (config.prompt). It is the full persona, behavior, and guardrail definition. Falls back to description when omitted.

tools.name: update_ai_agent
tools.description: Update an existing AI Agent: its identity fields (name, persona in description, guardrails in instructions) and its AI Agent Job Node config (jobConfig: job name, scope, procedures, LLM, temperature, maxTokens) in one call. Only the fields you pass change. Spread configuration across the matching fields rather than putting everything into description; the agent-prompts skill has the layout and writing rules. To give the agent knowledge, use create_tool with toolType 'knowledge' instead of persona text. Requires aiAgentId (from create_ai_agent or list_resources { resourceType: 'agent' }).

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID (from create_ai_agent response or list_resources)

description.description: Agent PERSONA (max 1000 chars) — who the agent is, who it serves, and its personality as behaviors, in prose, no headings or lists. Example: 'You are the order assistant for Acme Outdoor's online store. You help customers track orders and start returns. You're friendly and efficient: acknowledge a problem in one sentence, then fix it.'

instructions.description: COMMUNICATION and GUARDRAILS that apply regardless of the job (keep near 1000 chars): '## Communication' and '## Guardrails' sections, one rule per bullet. Don't restate Safety Settings rules. Example: '## Guardrails\n- Help only with Acme orders, returns and products.\n- Never share another customer's details.'

jobConfig.description: AI Agent Job Node configuration — the job role, scope, procedures, LLM, and model parameters. Fill the fields the agent needs, each fact in one field.

jobName.description: Job TITLE — the role the agent is performing. Example: 'Customer Support Specialist', 'Sales Assistant', 'Technical Advisor'

jobDescription.description: Job SCOPE in prose — every topic the job covers and what goes elsewhere. Tool details belong in the tool descriptions. Example: 'You handle order tracking, delivery questions, returns within 30 days and product questions. Payment disputes go to the support team.'

jobInstructions.description:
How to do the job, in '##' sections: Conversation flow, Using tools, When something goes wrong, Handing over, Voice output. Number only steps that happen in order; rules that apply any time are bullets. Example: '## Conversation flow
1. Find out what the customer needs.
2. Get the order number and look it up.

## Using tools
- Say one short line before a lookup, and vary it.
- If a tool fails, try once more, then offer the support team.'

llmProviderReferenceId.description: LLM referenceId to assign (from setup_llm or list_resources { resourceType: 'llm_model' }). Determines which LLM generates responses.

temperature.description: LLM temperature (0-1). Lower = more deterministic, higher = more creative. Default: 0.7

maxTokens.description: Max tokens for LLM response (100-8000). Default: 4000

tools.name: setup_llm
tools.description: Create a NEW LLM resource in a project, auto-creating a Connection from the provider credentials or reusing a same-project connectionId, then test the connection with a minimal probe. Use it only when no existing LLM can be reused via manage_packages; provider names, model strings, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and AWS Bedrock are covered by the llm-providers skill. Credentials are apiKey for most providers and accessKeyId + secretAccessKey or roleArn (plus region) for awsBedrock. Never invent credentials: if none and no connectionId were given, ask the user. A failed connection test deletes the model and returns an error; an untestable provider keeps it with a warning. Returns the LLM's referenceId, which update_ai_agent jobConfig.llmProviderReferenceId takes when isDefault is false.

provider.description: LLM provider (exact camelCase API value). Use 'openAICompatible' for any endpoint that speaks the OpenAI API (vLLM, Hugging Face, LiteLLM, Azure AI Foundry, ...); 'awsBedrock' for models on AWS Bedrock.

modelType.description: Model type string, e.g. chat 'gpt-4o', 'claude-sonnet-4-0', embedding 'text-embedding-3-small'. openAICompatible requires 'custom-model' (chat) or 'custom-embedding-model' (embedding), with the real name in customModel. awsBedrock takes a supported Bedrock model id (e.g. 'amazon.nova-pro-v1:0'; list in the llm-providers skill) or 'custom-model' + customModel.

name.description: Display name for the LLM resource. If omitted, defaults to customModel when provided (openAICompatible, or awsBedrock with modelType 'custom-model'), otherwise to modelType.

apiKey.description: Provider API key. A Connection will be auto-created from this key. Not used by awsBedrock — pass accessKeyId + secretAccessKey or roleArn there instead.

connectionId.description: Existing Connection referenceId (UUID) from the SAME project. Connections are project-scoped; to reuse one from another project, transfer it with manage_packages instead of passing it here.

baseCustomUrl.description: openAICompatible only (required): base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API, e.g. 'https://my-llm-host.example.com/v1'.

customModel.description: The provider's own model name when modelType is 'custom-model'. Required for openAICompatible (e.g. 'llama-3.3-70b-instruct'); optional for awsBedrock (a Bedrock model id or inference profile id, e.g. 'eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6').

customAuthHeader.description: openAICompatible only (optional): custom HTTP header name for authentication, e.g. 'X-Custom-Auth' or 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key'. When set, the API key is sent in this header instead of 'Authorization: Bearer'.

apiType.description: API flavor for chat models (openAI, azureOpenAI, openAICompatible only). Default: 'chatCompletion'. Use 'responses' only if the provider supports OpenAI's Responses API.

region.description: awsBedrock only (required): AWS region of the Bedrock deployment, e.g. 'us-east-1' or 'eu-central-1'.

location.description: awsBedrock only: inference-call routing. 'region' (default) keeps requests in the given region; 'geo' routes within a geographic boundary (requires geo); 'global' routes worldwide for the highest throughput.

geo.description: awsBedrock only, required when location is 'geo': the geographic boundary requests may be routed within, e.g. 'us', 'eu', or 'apac'. The AWS region must lie inside this boundary.

accessKeyId.description: awsBedrock only: AWS access key ID. Must be provided together with secretAccessKey. A Connection is auto-created from the pair.

secretAccessKey.description: awsBedrock only: AWS secret access key. Must be provided together with accessKeyId.

roleArn.description: awsBedrock only: IAM role ARN for role-based auth (alternative to accessKeyId + secretAccessKey), e.g. 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/cognigy-bedrock'. Feature-gated: the platform rejects this connection type unless IAM connections are enabled for the installation — prefer the access-key pair unless the user asked for IAM-role auth.

dangerouslySkipConnectionTest.description: Skip the connection test after creating the model (default: false). Last resort for providers whose test endpoint is known to be unreachable, and only with the user's explicit confirmation. A failed test means wrong credentials or a missing connection; skipping hides that rather than fixing it.

tools.name: talk_to_agent
tools.description: Send one message to a Cognigy AI Agent through its REST endpoint and return the reply, for testing during iterative development. Pass endpointId (from create_ai_agent or list_resources { resourceType: 'endpoint' }; the tool reads the token itself), or aiAgentId to have the tool find or create a REST endpoint for the agent's flow. endpointUrl is still accepted but is a credential, so prefer endpointId. Reuse the returned sessionId across calls for a multi-turn conversation. The project needs a working LLM, otherwise the reply is empty. Messages go through Cognigy Endpoint Test Mode by default, which is not billed (fair use: about 600 test messages per hour); testMode: false is billable and needs the user's consent. A failed send is never re-sent automatically, because it may already have run; its hints say how to check before retrying. Returns agentResponse, sessionId, endpointId when known and testMode, never the endpoint URL; verbose: true adds the raw API response.

endpointUrl.description: Full REST endpoint URL (the token is a credential). Accepted for compatibility; prefer endpointId. Takes precedence over endpointId and aiAgentId.

endpointId.description: 24-char hex ID of a REST endpoint (from create_ai_agent or list_resources { resourceType: 'endpoint' }). The tool looks up the token itself. Takes precedence over aiAgentId.

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID. When endpointUrl and endpointId are omitted, the tool finds or auto-creates a REST endpoint for this agent's flow.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Pass alongside aiAgentId when known (returned by create_ai_agent and list_resources) — saves a server-side lookup that can fail. Not used when endpointUrl or endpointId is provided.

message.description: Message to send to the agent

sessionId.description: Session ID for conversation continuity. Omit to start new session.

data.description: Additional data payload to send with the message

verbose.description: If true, include the full raw API response (default: false)

testMode.description: Send via Cognigy Endpoint Test Mode (default: true) so the message is not counted as billable. Set false only when the user explicitly wants a real, billable production message, or when a test-mode failure has been traced to a platform without test mode (older than Cognigy 4.27), the original message is confirmed unprocessed, and the user accepts the billing.

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: List Cognigy resources of one type, paginated, with optional server-side sort. Types: project (no projectId needed), tool (takes aiAgentId, or flowId for an LLM Prompt flow, instead of projectId), audit_event (organisation-wide, no projectId; answers "who changed what" via actor and eventType; Cognigy 2026.17.0+), log (read-only project logs, typically about 24 hours deep: read the default summary first, then narrow with search, logLevel, flowName, startDate/endDate or sessionId; view 'entries' for lines, msgChars up to 4000; scrubbed best-effort, may still hold personal data; the troubleshooting skill has the recipe), conversation (newest first, metadata only; read one with get_resource), and the project-scoped agent, flow, endpoint, llm_model, knowledge_store, extension, function. Endpoints show hasToken, not the URL token (revealToken: true if needed). Packages and snapshots: manage_packages, manage_snapshots. For recency questions use sort (e.g. 'lastChanged:desc', small limit).

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Required for all types except 'project', 'tool' and 'audit_event'.

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID (tools only — lists tools in the agent's flow)

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID (tools only) — alternative to aiAgentId for flows driven by an LLM Prompt node, which have no agent resource. Never pass both.

startDate.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, inclusive (log and conversation only)

endDate.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, inclusive (log and conversation only)

useCase.description: llm_model only — filter LLMs to the models allowed for a specific use case, matching the Cognigy UI dropdown. Example: 'knowledgeSearch', 'answerExtraction', 'aiAgent', or 'promptNode'.

sort.description: Server-side sort as 'field:direction', e.g. 'lastChanged:desc' or 'name:asc'. Sort on any field the resource returns. Not supported for 'tool' (read from the flow chart, not a list endpoint).

actor.description: audit_event only: who performed the action. 'mcp-plugin' is this plugin, 'ask-ai' the Cognigy Ask AI agent, 'human' a person in the UI or API. Filtered server-side on Cognigy 2026.17.0+, otherwise on the fetched page.

eventType.description: audit_event only: operation type filter. Filtered server-side on Cognigy 2026.17.0+, otherwise on the fetched page.

user.description: audit_event only — filter by the email of the user the action ran as.

logLevel.description: log only — keep only these levels. Request debug or trace here if you need them.

search.description: log only — substring match on the log message (not on metadata). Not allowed with sessionId.

flowName.description: log and conversation only — exact, case-sensitive flow name.

minMessages.description: conversation only — keep conversations with at least this many messages.

contactIds.description: conversation only — keep conversations of these contact ids (the one filter the platform applies itself).

sessionId.description: log only — read the newest logs of one conversation session (e.g. the sessionId from talk_to_agent). Cannot be combined with startDate, endDate, search, sort, skip or limit.

view.description: log only — 'summary' (default) returns level counts, time span, the most frequent message templates and flows; 'entries' returns individual entries with msg scrubbed best-effort (limit 1-100, page with skip).

msgChars.description: log only — per-message character cap for the 'entries' view (also with sessionId and view 'entries'), 100-4000, default 500. Messages are still scrubbed best-effort and may contain personal data. Ignored by the summary view.

rawMessages.description: log only, view 'entries' — return messages with URL queries or JSON bodies instead of a safe template. Still scrubbed best-effort; may contain personal data.

revealToken.description: endpoint only — include the URL token and endpoint URL, which are credentials: anyone holding the token can send messages to the endpoint. Default false (items show hasToken instead). Use only when a URL is really needed; talk_to_agent takes endpointId.

limit.description: Results per page (1-100, default 25). For log, only the 'entries' view.

skip.description: Number of results to skip (default 0). For log, pages the 'entries' view.

tools.name: get_resource
tools.description: Get one Cognigy resource by id, as a filtered summary by default or the complete API response with raw: true. Supports every list_resources type plus session_state (session context by session id) and user, where id 'me' returns the account the API key belongs to and a 24-char hex id another user. createdBy / lastChangedBy (returned only with raw: true) are opaque user ids: compare them with 'me' rather than guessing who they are. An audit_event carries performedBy. A conversation (id = session id) returns an outline of its messages by default; view 'text' adds scrubbed text (best-effort, may hold personal data; msgChars, rawText for unmasked), expertMode adds intents, limit and skip page the messages. Endpoints leave out the URL token and endpoint URL, also with raw: true (hasToken instead; revealToken: true restores them). Use list_resources first to find ids.

id.description: Resource ID (24-char hex, a session ID for conversation/session_state, or 'me' for resourceType 'user')

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Required for endpoint lookups.

raw.description: If true, return unfiltered API response (default: false)

view.description: conversation only — 'outline' (default: type, source, time, length) or 'text' (message text masked best-effort: names and addresses are not masked, it may contain personal data).

expertMode.description: conversation only — add intent and intentScore.

rawText.description: conversation only, view 'text' — unmasked text; only when scrubbing hides what you need.

msgChars.description: conversation only, view 'text' — characters kept per message (default 500).

revealToken.description: endpoint only — include the URL token and endpoint URL (also with raw: true), which are credentials: anyone holding the token can send messages to the endpoint. Default false (hasToken is shown instead). Use only when a URL is really needed; talk_to_agent takes endpointId.

tools.name: delete_resource
tools.description: Delete a Cognigy resource, or mark it for manual deletion. agent, flow and project are never hard-deleted: they are renamed with a DELETE_ prefix (idempotent; the response reports markedForDeletion or alreadyMarked), and agent and flow deletion also deactivate their endpoints, reversibly, unless cascade is false. endpoint, llm_model, knowledge_store, function and tool are permanently deleted and cannot be undone; tool additionally needs aiAgentId (or flowId for an LLM Prompt flow). Flow nodes are deleted with manage_flow_nodes and snapshots with manage_snapshots, not here.

resourceType.description: Type of resource to delete (flow/project/agent are renamed with a DELETE_ prefix instead of being deleted)

id.description: 24-char hex resource ID (or toolId for tool type)

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID (required for some types)

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID (tool type — needed to resolve the flow; required unless flowId is provided)

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID (tool type only) — alternative to aiAgentId for flows driven by an LLM Prompt node, which have no agent resource. Never pass both.

cascade.description: Agent deletion only. If true (default), deactivates the agent's endpoints and renames its flow and the agent with the DELETE_ prefix. If false, renames only the agent.

tools.name: manage_knowledge
tools.description: Manage Knowledge AI stores for RAG. Operations: create_store, create_source (type 'url' scrapes a page, 'manual' stores text, 'file' uploads a local PDF/TXT/DOCX/CTXT/PPTX; ingestion is async), list_sources (with chunkCount), delete_source (removes one source and its chunks), and list_chunks to verify what was ingested. The project needs an embedding model and Knowledge AI settings (manage_settings set_knowledge_ai) before a store is created; the knowledge-setup skill has the order. Stores are listed with list_resources and deleted with delete_resource. Attach a store to an agent with create_tool toolType 'knowledge'.

operation.description: create_store: new knowledge base. create_source: add content from URL, text, or file. list_chunks: list/filter chunks in a source. list_sources: list all sources in a knowledge store. delete_source: remove one source and its chunks.

knowledgeStoreId.description: 24-char hex store ID (required for create_source, list_chunks, list_sources, delete_source)

sourceId.description: 24-char hex source ID (required for delete_source; optional for list_chunks — if omitted, uses the first source in the store)

name.description: Source or store name (required for create_store, optional for create_source)

type.description: Source type (create_source). 'url' scrapes a web page. 'manual' stores text directly. 'file' uploads a local document. Auto-detected from provided fields if omitted.

url.description: URL to scrape (required when type is url)

text.description: Text content to store as a knowledge chunk (required when type is manual)

filePath.description: Absolute path to a local file to upload (required when type is file). Supported formats: PDF, TXT, DOCX, CTXT, PPTX. Max 10MB. Example: '/Users/me/docs/report.pdf'.

filter.description: Text filter for list_chunks — matches against chunk text

tools.name: create_tool
tools.description: Add a tool to an AI Agent's Job Node so the agent's LLM can call it. toolType: 'tool' (default: a custom logic branch you fill with manage_flow_nodes afterwards), 'http' (call a concrete REST endpoint, with optional pre/post-process Code nodes), 'knowledge' (search a Knowledge Store), 'send_email', 'mcp' (only for an explicitly named external MCP server URL), or 'a2a' (delegate to a remote A2A agent outside the project, or on an explicit A2A request). One tool per business action: an existing toolId is reused, never duplicated. For an LLM Prompt flow pass flowId instead of aiAgentId; it supports only tool, http and mcp. Cognigy runtime conventions for http and Code nodes are in the parameter descriptions and the tools-setup skill. Returns toolNodeId and child node ids for update_tool and manage_flow_nodes.

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID (from create_ai_agent or list_resources { resourceType: 'agent' }). Required unless flowId is provided.

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID — use instead of aiAgentId only for LLM Prompt flows with no agent resource. Never pass both.

parentNodeId.description: 24-char hex node ID of the AI Agent Job or LLM Prompt node the tool attaches to. Only needed when the flow has more than one node of the preferred type, or when a flow addressed by flowId holds both an AI Agent Job node and an LLM Prompt node — create_tool then refuses to guess and lists the candidates. The chosen parent comes back as parentNodeId/parentNodeType.

toolType.description: tool (default), knowledge, send_email, mcp, http or a2a; see the tool description for when each applies. LLM Prompt nodes support only tool, mcp and http.

name.description: Tool display name (e.g., 'Fetch Weather', 'Search FAQ'). The node label in the flow uses the snake_case toolId from config (e.g., 'fetch_weather') if provided, otherwise falls back to this name.

config.description: Tool-specific configuration — fields depend on toolType.

toolId.description: Tool identifier for the LLM in snake_case (e.g., fetch_weather, search_faq). Also used as the node label in the flow. (tool, knowledge, send_email, http)

description.description: Tool description for the LLM (tool, knowledge, send_email, http): what it does, when to use it and when not to, in 1-3 sentences (see the agent-prompts skill)

parameters.description: JSON Schema string for the tool parameters (tool, http). Top level must be {"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}: "required" is mandatory (use [] if none), every property needs "type" and "description", arrays need "items", nested objects their own "required". "additionalProperties": false is added automatically. Strict-mode models (OpenAI Responses API) need every key in "required", optional ones nullable.

topK.description: Number of results to return (knowledge only, default varies)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. For mcp: connection timeout. For a2a: Agent Card discovery timeout (mcp, a2a only)

headers.description: HTTP headers as key-value pairs, e.g. { "Authorization": "Bearer ..." } (http only)

body.description: Request body template (http only). In a JSON body, inline {{input.aiAgent.toolArgs.x}} always sends a STRING; for a number, boolean, array or object field use { "$cs": { "script": "<bare expression>", "type": "number" } } instead (no {{ }} inside the script, type optional, $cs the only key on its object). Example: {"name": "{{input.aiAgent.toolArgs.name}}", "qty": { "$cs": { "script": "input.aiAgent.toolArgs.qty", "type": "number" } }}

preProcessCode.description: JavaScript for a Code node that runs BEFORE the HTTP request (http only). Cognigy Code-node rules: no top-level return, mutate input / context directly; the LLM's tool arguments are at input.aiAgent.toolArgs.<param>, not input.data. The runtime has no api.httpRequest, fetch, require/import (moment, _, xmljs are globals) or api.setState/getState; such code is written anyway and flagged in _hints.warning.

postProcessCode.description: JavaScript for a Code node that runs AFTER the HTTP response (http only). input.httprequest is an object { result, statusCode, length }, not the raw body; no top-level return; store what the LLM should see where toolResponseValue reads it. Same runtime limits as preProcessCode.

logToolCalls.description: Default true: a Log node is written at the HEAD of the tool branch recording the tool name and its parameter NAMES (never values — tool arguments routinely carry personal data). At the head so a call that later throws or hangs has still been logged. Level is info, so it appears without enabling the Debug log filter. Set false to skip it.

toolResponseValue.description: CognigyScript expression for the Resolve Tool Action node's answer, i.e. what the LLM receives as the tool result. Defaults: '{{JSON.stringify(input.httprequest)}}' for http tools, '{{JSON.stringify(input.result)}}' for general tools. Set it to wherever your code stores the result.

agentBaseUrl.description: Base URL of the remote A2A agent: whatever base URL an external agent publishes. For a Cognigy agent behind manage_a2a_server, use that tool's returned agentBaseUrl verbatim (it carries the required /a2a/v1/<URLToken> path); never build it from the endpoint's plain URL (a2a only)

agentCardPath.description: Path to the remote agent's Agent Card, appended to agentBaseUrl for discovery. Default: '.well-known/agent.json' (a2a only)

executionMode.description: How the delegated task runs, e.g. 'blocking' (wait for the remote agent's final result). Default: 'blocking' (a2a only)

taskTimeout.description: Max seconds to wait for the remote agent's task to complete (a2a only)

maxAutonomousTurns.description: How many times the AI Agent may call this tool in one turn (1-10). Default: 4 (a2a only)

toolFilter.description: Which of the remote agent's skills are listed in this tool's description. Default: 'none' (all skills). NOT an access control: the node stays one tool and the remote agent still decides which skills it runs (a2a only)

whitelist.description: Skill ids to list in the tool description when toolFilter is 'whitelist' (a2a only)

blacklist.description: Skill ids to leave out of the tool description when toolFilter is 'blacklist' (a2a only)

authType.description: Authentication method for calling the remote agent. Default: 'none' (a2a only)

apiKeyConnection.description: Connection ID holding the API key, when authType is 'apiKey'. Connections are project-scoped — must be from the same project as the agent (a2a only)

apiKeyHeader.description: Header name for the API key, when authType is 'apiKey'. Default: 'X-API-Key'. A Cognigy a2aServer target expects 'x-a2a-endpoint-key' (a2a only)

bearerConnection.description: Connection ID holding the bearer token, when authType is 'bearer'. Connections are project-scoped — must be from the same project as the agent (a2a only)

basicConnection.description: Connection ID holding basic-auth credentials, when authType is 'basic'. Connections are project-scoped — must be from the same project as the agent (a2a only)

oAuth2Connection.description: Connection ID for OAuth2, when authType is 'oAuth2'. Connections are project-scoped — must be from the same project as the agent (a2a only)

authForDiscovery.description: Whether to also apply authType when fetching the Agent Card during discovery, not just when calling tasks (a2a only)

agentHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers to send to the remote agent, as a JSON string, e.g. '{"X-Trace-Id":"..."}' (a2a only)

cacheCard.description: Cache the discovered Agent Card instead of re-fetching it on every call. Default: true (a2a only)

tools.name: update_tool
tools.description: Update an existing tool node on an AI Agent: its display name and any config field create_tool accepts, merged into the current config. For http tools url, method, headers and body update the child HTTP Request node, and preProcessCode / postProcessCode update or create the child Code nodes; pass httpNodeId, preProcessNodeId, postProcessNodeId or resolveNodeId to target a specific child when label lookup is ambiguous. Requires toolNodeId (from create_tool or list_resources { resourceType: 'tool', aiAgentId }) and aiAgentId, or flowId for an LLM Prompt flow.

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID (from create_ai_agent or list_resources { resourceType: 'agent' }). Required unless flowId is provided.

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID — alternative to aiAgentId, ONLY for flows driven by an LLM Prompt node (no agent resource exists for those). Never pass both.

toolNodeId.description: 24-char hex tool node ID (from create_tool or list_resources { resourceType: 'tool', aiAgentId })

name.description: New display name for the tool node (optional)

toolType.description: Tool type hint — helps the handler know which config fields to map. Optional if only updating name.

config.description: Tool-specific configuration — same fields as create_tool config. Merged with existing config on the node.

toolId.description: Tool identifier for the LLM (tool, knowledge, send_email, http)

description.description: Tool description for the LLM (tool, knowledge, send_email, http): what it does, when to use it and when not to, in 1-3 sentences (see the agent-prompts skill)

parameters.description: JSON Schema string for the tool parameters (tool, http). Same contract as create_tool config.parameters.

topK.description: Number of results to return (knowledge only)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. For mcp: connection timeout. For a2a: Agent Card discovery timeout (mcp, a2a only)

headers.description: HTTP headers as key-value pairs (http only)

preProcessCode.description: JavaScript code for the pre-process Code node (http only). Same runtime notes as create_tool's preProcessCode; code using an unavailable API is written anyway and flagged in _hints.warning.

postProcessCode.description: JavaScript code for the post-process Code node (http only). Same runtime notes as preProcessCode.

toolResponseValue.description: CognigyScript expression for the Resolve Tool Action node's answer (what the LLM receives). Defaults as in create_tool.

httpNodeId.description: Optional 24-char hex id of the HTTP Request child node (from create_tool childNodes), when label lookup fails (http only).

preProcessNodeId.description: Optional 24-char hex id of the pre-process Code child node (from create_tool childNodes), when label lookup fails (http only).

postProcessNodeId.description: Optional 24-char hex id of the post-process Code child node (from create_tool childNodes), when label lookup fails (http only).

resolveNodeId.description: Optional 24-char hex id of the Resolve Tool Action child node (from create_tool childNodes). Needed for toolResponseValue when the flow has more than one such node.

agentBaseUrl.description: Base URL of the remote A2A agent. Use manage_a2a_server's `agentBaseUrl` response field verbatim for a Cognigy agent — do not use its `endpointId`'s plain URL (a2a only)

agentCardPath.description: Path to the remote agent's Agent Card, appended to agentBaseUrl (a2a only)

executionMode.description: How the delegated task runs (a2a only)

taskTimeout.description: Max seconds to wait for the remote agent's task (a2a only)

maxAutonomousTurns.description: How many times the AI Agent may call this tool in one turn (1-10) (a2a only)

toolFilter.description: Which remote skills are listed in the tool description. Not an access control (a2a only)

whitelist.description: Skill ids to list in the tool description (a2a only)

blacklist.description: Skill ids to leave out of the tool description (a2a only)

authType.description: Authentication method for calling the remote agent (a2a only)

apiKeyConnection.description: Connection ID for apiKey auth. Connections are project-scoped (a2a only)

apiKeyHeader.description: Header name for the API key. A Cognigy a2aServer target expects 'x-a2a-endpoint-key' (a2a only)

bearerConnection.description: Connection ID for bearer auth. Connections are project-scoped (a2a only)

basicConnection.description: Connection ID for basic auth. Connections are project-scoped (a2a only)

oAuth2Connection.description: Connection ID for OAuth2. Connections are project-scoped (a2a only)

authForDiscovery.description: Also authenticate when fetching the Agent Card (a2a only)

agentHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers to send, as a JSON string (a2a only)

cacheCard.description: Cache the discovered Agent Card (a2a only)

tools.name: manage_flows
tools.description: Create, rename and clone Flows, or give one a REST endpoint. Use it for a Flow that is not an AI Agent (shared subroutine, error handler, classic dialog) or a second Flow in a project; create_ai_agent provisions its own Flow, so do not call this first when building an agent. Operations: create (empty Flow with Start and End; needs projectId and name; returns the flow id and referenceId; add logic with manage_flow_nodes), update (rename or change the description; needs flowId plus name and/or description), clone (copy a Flow with its nodes in the same project; needs flowId), create_endpoint (reuse or create the REST endpoint serving the Flow; needs flowId, optional name; returns endpointId, never the URL or token). A Flow's referenceId (a UUID, not the 24-char hex id) is what executeFlow and goTo nodes point at, passed as flowId.

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID (required for update, clone and create_endpoint). This is the id, not the referenceId UUID.

name.description: Flow name (required for create, optional for update). Endpoint name for create_endpoint (optional, defaults to '<flow name> REST Endpoint'). Shown in the Cognigy UI.

description.description: What the flow is for (optional). Worth setting on shared flows so the next person knows when it runs.

tools.name: manage_flow_nodes
tools.description: Manage the logic nodes inside a Cognigy flow and render the flow as a diagram. Operations: list (id, referenceId, type, label, parentId, isDisabled when true, ordered children and next; no config; a partial list says truncated), get (one node with config; fields and saveTo pull large fields out, saveTo into a file instead of the reply), create (nodeType + config, placed by parentNodeId and mode), update (partial config or label; cases for switch/lookup nodes; configFromFiles loads large values from files), compare (a node field against a file: equality, sizes, hashes, never content), delete, render (read-only ascii tree plus mermaid string). Nodes belong inside a tool branch: create the tool first and pass parentNodeId = toolNodeId with mode 'appendChild'; never add standalone nodes before the AI Agent Job Node. The exception is llmPrompt, created only when the user asks for one by name. Node types, config schemas, file rules and Go To referenceIds are in the flow-nodes skill.

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID (from create_ai_agent response or list_resources { resourceType: 'flow' })

nodeId.description: 24-char hex node ID (required for get, update, and delete)

nodeType.description: Node type key (required for create). The authoritative set comes from the server node registry; an unsupported value returns an error listing the current types. Common types: say, question, ifThenElse, lookup, setSessionContext, code, goTo, sleep, wait (Wait for Input), httpRequest. CXone Agent Copilot: cxOneSendCopilotStatus. xApp nodes: initAppSession, showXAppAdaptiveCard, showXAppHtml, setXAppState, getXAppSessionPin.

label.description: Display label for the node (required for create, optional for update). Pass only the descriptive part: the plugin adds the naming-convention prefix for the node type (say "Greeting" → "Say: Greeting"; also Q:, Code:, ATC:, RTA:, If:, HTTP:, Log:, Switch:, GoTo:, Wait:, LLM:, Config:, xApp:). For if nodes, name the value being checked. Execute Flow nodes are named after their target flow. A label with the right prefix is kept.

comment.description: The node's Comment in the Cognigy editor (create/update; "" clears it). Optional: add one only where the flow is complex enough that a reader needs the why — a non-obvious branch, an ordering dependency, a workaround. Keep it to 1-2 sentences.

parentNodeId.description: Target node ID. Set to the tool node ID (from create_tool) and use mode=appendChild to add nodes inside a tool branch. Use mode=append to place after a sibling node.

mode.description: Placement mode: appendChild (inside target — use this to add nodes under a tool) or append (after target as a sibling). Default: append.

errorTrace.description: code nodes only (create/update). Default true: the plugin adds error handling around the code — on a throw it logs a standard trace to the project logs and input.errorTrace / context.lastError / context.errors, then sets input.hasError. Just write the code; get returns it without the added handling. Set false only to write the code with no error handling added.

errorGuard.description: code nodes only (create). Default true: an `if {{input.hasError}}` guard is appended after the node. Its then-branch is left empty — it is a branch point for the active flow to handle the failure, not a logger (the error is already logged). Set false to keep the error handling but skip the guard.

errorHandlerFlowId.description: code nodes only (create), optional. Reference ID of a shared flow to run from the guard's then-branch as a side trip (a ticket, a webhook, a notification). Uses Execute Flow, which RETURNS, so the active flow still owns the user-facing experience. Omit unless the project has such a flow.

focus.description: render only: node ID (or an array of node IDs) to highlight in the diagram (e.g. nodes you just created or edited).

format.description: render only: which representation(s) to return. Default: both.

legend.description: render only: include a key of only the shapes/edges present in this flow (embedded in the mermaid + returned as `legend` rows + shown in the HTML). Default: true.

writeHtml.description: render only: also write a self-contained HTML graph to a tmp file on the user's machine and return htmlUrl / htmlPath. Default: false.

openInBrowser.description: render only (requires writeHtml): open the generated HTML in the user's default browser automatically. Default: true — set false to only get htmlUrl/htmlPath back without opening.

fields.description: get only: dotted paths into the node (e.g. config.code, config.instructions, label); returns just those plus id. Missing paths are listed in missingFields.

saveTo.description: get only: field path -> file path. Each key must also be in `fields`. The string value is written to the file (inside the working directory, max 2 MiB, UTF-8) and replaced in the result by { savedTo, bytes, sha256 }.

overwrite.description: get with saveTo: replace files that already exist. Default: false (an existing file is an error).

configFromFiles.description: update only: top-level config key -> file path (max 20). The file text becomes config[key]. A key may not also appear in `config`. No API call is made if any file fails.

field.description: compare only: dotted path of the string field to compare, e.g. config.code.

file.description: compare only: file (inside the working directory) to compare the field with.

tools.name: manage_packages
tools.description: Export and import Cognigy package .zip files with the same staged workflow as the UI, including moving an LLM together with its Connection between projects. Operations: list_exportable, export (saves the zip locally, dependencies included by default), download (saves an existing package), upload_and_inspect (upload a local zip and return the import preview), inspect (preview an uploaded packageId), import (merge selected resources with UI-parity defaults: 're-identify', knowledge stores 'replace'), read_task (poll a long-running task). Import and export wait for completion by default. Export and download return the absolute saved path and file:// URIs; show them to the user verbatim.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID for the package import/export workflow.

filePath.description: Absolute path to a local package `.zip` file. Required for upload_and_inspect.

packageId.description: 24-char hex package ID. Required for inspect, import, and download.

taskId.description: 24-char hex task ID. Required for read_task.

resourceIds.description: Resource IDs to export into a package. Required for export.

dependencyResourceIds.description: Optional dependency resource IDs to include during export. If omitted, all detected dependencies are included by default.

includeDependencies.description: When true (default), export includes detected dependencies for the selected resources.

name.description: Base package name for export. A timestamp suffix is appended automatically for UI parity.

outputPath.description: Absolute local file path or directory where the exported `.zip` should be saved. Used by export and download. If omitted, a temp path is created automatically.

resources.description: Optional resource selections for import. If omitted, preview defaults are used.

id.description: 24-char hex resource ID from the package preview.

import.description: Whether to import the resource. Default: true unless disabled in preview.

localeMapping.description: Optional locale mapping overrides for import.

waitForCompletion.description: When true (default), wait for import/export task completion.

tools.name: manage_webchat
tools.description: Create or update a Webchat v3 endpoint that deploys an agent's flow as an embeddable website chat widget. Without endpointId a new endpoint is created (projectId and flowId required); with endpointId the existing endpoint is updated and the given settings are merged, so pass only what should change. stylePreset applies a predefined look, the setting groups (layout, behavior, startBehavior, homeScreen, ...) cover the Webchat settings, and customJson takes anything else. Always returns demoWebchatUrl, a live test page to show the user as a link, plus _integration with the embed snippet.

endpointId.description: 24-char hex endpoint ID. If provided, updates the existing endpoint. If omitted, creates a new endpoint.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Required for create, optional for update.

flowId.description: Flow referenceId to connect the webchat endpoint to. Required for create.

stylePreset.description: Apply a predefined style. classic: compact 460px. modern: wide 900px with streaming. slick: medium 600px with grey bubbles.

layout.description: Visual layout: title, logo, chat window size, bot output width, input behavior, HTML settings, agent avatars.

maxInputRows.description: Max lines in reply field before scrollbar

enableInputCollation.description: Combine rapid inputs into one message

allowJsInHtml.description: Allow JS in HTML messages (security risk)

useAgentAvatars.description: Show separate avatar/name for bot vs human

behavior.description: Chat behavior: scrolling, streaming, markdown, typing indicators, STT/TTS, message delay.

collateStreamedOutputs.description: Merge streamed text into one bubble

renderMarkdown.description: Render markdown in bot outputs (default: true)

startBehavior.description: How conversation starts: text field, button click, or auto-send.

homeScreen.description: Home screen with welcome message, background, conversation starters, and previous conversations.

teaserMessage.description: Teaser message beside webchat icon with optional conversation starters.

chatOptions.description: Chat options menu: quick replies, TTS toggle, conversation rating, footer links.

privacyNotice.description: Privacy notice shown before chat begins.

businessHours.description: Restrict webchat availability to business hours.

customJson.description: Raw JSON string for advanced Webchat Custom Settings not covered by other fields.

tools.name: manage_voice_gateway
tools.description: Create or update a Voice Gateway endpoint with a WebRTC client so users can talk to an agent from the browser. Without endpointId a new voiceGateway2 endpoint is created (projectId and flowId required); with endpointId the existing endpoint is updated and settings are merged. webrtcWidgetConfig customizes theme, transcription, avatar and tagline. Always returns webrtcDemoUrl, a live voice page, plus _integration with the WebSocket URL and embed snippet.

endpointId.description: 24-char hex endpoint ID. If provided, updates the existing endpoint. If omitted, creates a new endpoint.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Required for create, optional for update.

flowId.description: Flow referenceId to connect the voice gateway endpoint to. Required for create.

name.description: Endpoint display name (e.g. "Customer Support Voice Agent")

webrtcWidgetConfig.description: WebRTC widget appearance and behavior. Defaults are applied if omitted.

label.description: AI Agent name displayed in the widget

position.description: Widget position on demo page (default: centered)

avatarLogoUrl.description: URL for the agent avatar image

tagline.description: Short tagline displayed under the agent name

tools.name: manage_settings
tools.description: Set project-level Cognigy settings. set_voice_preview selects the speech provider for voice preview, auto-detecting a matching speech Connection when connectionId is omitted. set_knowledge_ai sets the Knowledge Search and Answer Extraction models and the content parser; model ids must be llm_model referenceIds from the SAME project (list_resources with useCase 'knowledgeSearch' matches the UI dropdown), and it runs before a knowledge store is created. get_knowledge_ai reads the Knowledge AI and generative AI settings (read-only). Details are in the settings and knowledge-setup skills.

provider.description: Speech provider to configure for voice preview

connectionId.description: Connection referenceId to use. If omitted, auto-detects an existing speech connection for the provider.

knowledgeSearchModelId.description: llm_model referenceId from the SAME project to use for Knowledge Search.

answerExtractionModelId.description: Optional llm_model referenceId from the SAME project to use for Answer Extraction.

contentParser.description: Content Parser to use for Knowledge AI document processing.

azureDIConnectionId.description: Azure AI Document Intelligence connection referenceId. Required when contentParser is azure.

tools.name: audit_voice_agent
tools.description: Audit a voice agent's flow, and optionally its endpoint and LLM, against the deterministic checks of the Voice AI Go-Live Checklist: Set Session Config first, barge-in and continuous ASR off, input and flow timeouts, streaming, error handling, latency logging, fallback LLM, STT hints, output transformer. Dry-run by default: each failing check reports a proposedFix and nothing changes. apply: true applies the safe fixes, optionally narrowed with only. Provide aiAgentId or flowId; endpointId and projectId enable the endpoint and LLM checks. Checks outside this subset are listed in the voice-go-live-checklist skill.

aiAgentId.description: 24-char hex AI Agent ID. The flow is resolved automatically. Provide this or flowId.

flowId.description: 24-char hex flow ID. Use instead of aiAgentId when the flow is known directly.

endpointId.description: 24-char hex endpoint ID (optional). When provided, the Output Transformer check is evaluated.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID (optional). When provided, the agent's LLM is resolved for the fallback check.

apply.description: If true, apply the safe auto-fixes for failing checks. Default false (dry-run report only).

only.description: Optional list of check IDs to apply when apply is true (e.g. ["vg.barge-in-off", "agent.stream-output"]). If omitted, all auto-fixable failing checks are applied.

tools.name: manage_snapshots
tools.description: Create, list, restore and delete Cognigy Snapshots: immutable, project-wide backups that let agent changes be rolled back. Operations: list (flags plugin-created backups and the count against the snapshot limit), create (waits for the task), restore (returns a preflight report until confirm is true), delete (plugin-created '[AI Backup]' snapshots only, never human ones), decline (record that the user refused a backup for this project), read_task. Restore deletes and recreates every resource in the project, changes all ids, and does not cover Endpoints or Knowledge AI. This is also the tool to call when another tool returns backup_not_offered. Error results such as snapshot_limit_reached or task_status_unknown carry the next step in their hints.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID the snapshot belongs to. Required for every operation.

snapshotId.description: 24-char hex snapshot ID. Required for restore and delete. Must belong to projectId.

limit.description: For list: how many snapshots to return (default 100). The reported count, atLimit and oldestDeletableBackup always describe the whole project, never just this page.

skip.description: For list: how many snapshots to skip (default 0).

taskId.description: 24-char hex task ID. Required for read_task.

label.description: Optional short label describing why the backup was taken, e.g. "pre-persona-update". Used inside the generated name; do NOT pass a full snapshot name.

confirmDeleteOldest.description: For create at the snapshot limit: when true, delete the OLDEST plugin-created backup to free a slot, then create. Set this only after the user has explicitly agreed. Default: false.

confirm.description: For restore: when true, actually perform the destructive restore. When false or omitted, restore only returns a preflight report and changes nothing. Set this only after the user has seen the preflight and agreed. Default: false.

waitForCompletion.description: When true (default), wait for the create/restore/delete task to finish.

timeoutMs.description: Task polling timeout in milliseconds (1000-3600000). Default: 600000. For create it is the budget for the WHOLE call, including any deletion needed to free a slot.

tools.name: manage_a2a_server
tools.description: Create or update an A2A Server Endpoint that exposes a flow as an Agent2Agent agent which other agents, Cognigy or third-party, discover and call (create_tool { toolType: 'a2a' } on the calling side). Use it only when the agent must be reachable from outside its project or the user asks for A2A; same-project agents use the native Handover to AI Agent tool. It creates a publicly callable endpoint, so confirm with the user first. Without endpointId a new endpoint is created (projectId and flowId required); with endpointId the existing one is updated and settings are merged. agentName, agentDescription and skills form the Agent Card. Returns agentBaseUrl, agentCardUrl and liveCheck, a live fetch of the Agent Card; surface liveCheck.reachable to the user, since a saved config is not proof the agent is callable. The a2a-setup skill covers the workflow.

endpointId.description: 24-char hex endpoint ID. If provided, updates the existing endpoint. If omitted, creates a new endpoint.

projectId.description: 24-char hex project ID. Required for create, optional for update.

flowId.description: Flow referenceId to connect the A2A server endpoint to. Required for create.

name.description: Endpoint display name (e.g. "Flights Agent A2A Server")

agentName.description: Name for this agent as shown in its Agent Card to remote callers

agentDescription.description: Description for this agent's Agent Card — what it does, for a remote orchestrator's LLM to decide when to delegate to it

skills.description: Skills this agent exposes in its Agent Card, e.g. [{ id: 'book-flight', name: 'book-flight', description: 'Book a flight' }]

enableStreaming.description: Stream partial results back to the calling agent

authenticationType.description: How callers must authenticate to this A2A server endpoint. Default: none

tools.name: manage_intents
tools.description: Read and manage the NLU intents of a flow (up to 3 levels: family, group, tag), including example sentences, and train the model. Reads: list (full, compact or summary view), get, export_tree, below_minimum, compare (against a CSV file), model_state. All write operations (create, update, move, delete, import_sentences and build) change the flow's NLU and are held by the backup gate until a backup is offered or declined. Never guess an intent: pass an id, a unique name or a Parent/Child path. import_csv and import_tree read sentences (and a tree spec) from project files so the text never passes through the conversation; both are held by the backup gate. Results never echo sentences or upstream errors.

projectId.description: Project ID; required for every write and must be the flow's project

intent.description: Intent id, unique name, or Parent/Child path (get, update, move, delete)

parent.description: Parent intent (id, name or path). On move, null makes the intent a root

childFeatures.description: Let the intent have child intents (create, update)

priority.description: Whether parent or child intents win on a tie

sentences.description: Example sentences for the new intent (create)

intent.description: Intent id, name or Parent/Child path

entries.description: import_sentences: sentences per intent (max 500 entries, 10000 sentences)

mode.description: import_sentences, import_csv: add or replace (required); import_tree default add. build: full or quick (default full)

file.description: compare, import_csv: CSV path inside the project (no header; intent,exampleSentence,sentence)

view.description: list: full (default, one object per intent), compact (a table) or summary (counts only, best for large flows)

includeSentences.description: get: also return the intent's sentences

sentencesFile.description: import_tree: optional CSV of tag sentences (same format as file)

createMissing.description: import_csv: create intents missing from the flow as roots (default true)

waitSeconds.description: build: seconds to wait for training (0-300, default 60)

deadlineSeconds.description: import_sentences: seconds before stopping a large import (1-600, default 60); re-run to finish
